item.mechanism: Severe lattice distortion due to random elemental distribution causes edge dislocation cores to deviate from neutral planes, creating wavy lines that impede screw dislocation motion and make edge dislocations the dominant mobile type.
item.system: NbTaTiV BCC refractory high-entropy alloy (nominal Nb25Ta25Ti25V25)
item.operating_conditions: Plastic deformation at room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 900°C) with macrostrains up to 15%
item.supporting_observation: Williamson-Hall peak-broadening analysis showed linear trends for edge dislocation models but nonmonotonous deviations for screw dislocation models; HAADF-STEM images visually confirmed the presence of edge dislocations.
item.scope_limits: This mechanism is specific to BCC HEAs with severely distorted lattices; it contrasts with conventional low-entropy BCC metals where screw dislocations typically dominate due to easy annihilation of edge dislocations.
item.alternatives_considered: Conventional BCC metals where screw dislocations are dominant due to low critical stress for edge dislocation movement and easy annihilation.
quotes: During the plastic deformation, the edge dislocation core can be deviated from their neutral dislocation planes, producing the wavy dislocation lines, which are attributed to the severe lattice distortion.

item.mechanism: The random distribution of multiple elements with different atomic radii leads to a severely distorted lattice, which minimizes the variation in diffraction elastic constants among grains, resulting in elastically isotropic deformation behavior at room temperature.
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature (RT) and elevated temperatures (500°C, 700°C, 900°C) under compressive loading
item.supporting_observation: In situ neutron diffraction showed nearly identical slopes for lattice strain evolution across different {hkl} planes at RT, and the universal elastic anisotropy index (AU) was calculated to be 0.
item.scope_limits: Elastic anisotropy gradually increases at elevated temperatures, though the variation is much smaller than in conventional alloys; the mechanism of perfect isotropy is most pronounced at RT.
item.alternatives_considered: Conventional BCC alloys which typically exhibit strong orientation-dependent lattice strain evolution and significant elastic anisotropy.
quotes: The random distribution of multiple elements with different atomic radii leads to a severely distorted lattice with variations in the interatomic distances along the crystallographic direction of the unit cells.
It was found that the variation in diffraction elastic constants among all the grains is not clearly observed, indicating the elastically isotropic deformation behavior.

item.mechanism: Homogeneous load sharing between differently oriented grains, resulting from reduced plastic anisotropy and simultaneous yielding at similar stress levels, leads to excellent ductility and prevents stress concentration.
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature compression with yield strength around 1000 MPa
item.supporting_observation: All oriented grains yielded at the same stress level (around 1000 MPa), and load transfer features were not clearly presented during plastic deformation, indicating reduced plastic anisotropy.
item.scope_limits: This behavior is specific to the unique elastic isotropy and dislocation characteristics of this HEA; conventional BCC alloys show inharmonic load partitioning leading to stress concentrations.
item.alternatives_considered: Conventional BCC alloys where {110} and {211} grains yield early, leading to load transfer to {200} grains and potential stress concentrations.
quotes: With this unusual elastic deformation, all orientated grains yield at the same stress level (around 1000 MPa).
Furthermore, the features of the load transfer were not clearly presented during plastic deformation at RT, indicating the reduced plastic anisotropy.
This trend of the reduced plastic anisotropic deformation behavior could result in the excellent ductility (plasticity) at RT because of the homogeneous load sharing between differently grains.

item.mechanism: The tetragonal shear modulus (C') is substantially reduced with decreasing elastic moduli, but C44 remains nearly constant, implying elastic stability against tetragonal shear deformation even as stiffness drops.
item.supporting_observation: Experimental data showed C11 and C12 drastically reduced at 900°C while C44 remained nearly constant, resulting in a small change in C' and indicating elastic stability.
item.scope_limits: This stability is observed up to 900°C; the mechanism relies on the specific temperature dependence of C11, C12, and C44 in this specific alloy.
item.alternatives_considered: Conventional alloys where elastic constants might degrade differently or lead to instability at high temperatures.
quotes: This result implies the elastic stability of this BCC HEA against the tetragonal shear deformation.

item.mechanism: The intrinsic ductility is predicted by the relationship between polycrystalline elastic moduli, specifically a high Pugh ratio (K/G > 1.75) and positive Cauchy pressure, indicating metallic bonding character and fracture resistance.
item.supporting_observation: Calculated Pugh ratios were >1.75 and Cauchy pressure was positive across all tested temperatures, suggesting intrinsic ductility.
item.scope_limits: This prediction relies on empirical criteria derived from bulk metallic glasses and polycrystalline materials; it assumes isotropic behavior for the Poisson's ratio criterion.
item.alternatives_considered: Brittle behavior associated with negative Cauchy pressure or low Pugh ratios (<1.75).
quotes: Hence, higher values of Pugh ratios (>1.75) indicate that the materials are ductile, whereas lower values are related to the brittle property.

item.mechanism: The Kroner self-consistent model accounts for the variation of stresses and strains among all grains, providing the most accurate determination of macroscopic elastic moduli from diffraction elastic moduli in HEA systems.
item.supporting_observation: The Kroner model showed the best agreement with experimental data (absolute percentage SEs of 2.46% to 8.85%) compared to Voigt and Reuss models.
item.scope_limits: The Voigt and Reuss models only consider homogeneous strains or stresses, respectively, and were found less suitable for this heterogeneous HEA system.
item.alternatives_considered: Voigt model (homogeneous strains) and Reuss model (homogeneous stresses).
quotes: These two theoretical models only consider homogeneous strains (Voigt) or stresses (Reuss) in all the grains during continuous loading.
On the other hand, the Kroner model accounts for the variation of stresses and strains among all the grains.

item.mechanism: Machine learning models using Holder means of elemental properties (group numbers, atomic radii, electronegativity) and structural properties (cohesive energy, density) can predict shear and bulk moduli for disordered HEAs with good accuracy.
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature (prediction based on training data from ordered compounds)
item.supporting_observation: The ML model predicted a shear modulus of 36.6 GPa and bulk modulus of 146.3 GPa, with relative errors of 2.5% and 6% compared to experimental values.
item.scope_limits: The model was trained on ordered compounds from the Materials Project database, not disordered alloys; the lattice distortion effect in HEAs might cause less accurate results, though agreement was good.
item.alternatives_considered: First-principles calculations (DFT) which showed larger deviations (-15.9% to -16.6% for Young's and shear moduli).
quotes: The set of elemental and structural properties that were found to be good predictions in the shear modulus ML model were the Holder mean (fourth power) of the group numbers of the elements, cohesive energy, the Holder mean (second power) of the atomic radii of the elements...
The predicted shear modulus is 36.6 GPa, and the predicted bulk modulus is 146.3 GPa, giving relative errors of 2.5 and 6%, respectively.
The good agreement suggests that these models may be useful for conservative estimates.

item.mechanism: The valence electron concentration (VEC) correlates with elastically isotropic deformation behavior in BCC refractory HEAs, with a VEC around 4.7 promoting isotropy.
item.system: NbTaTiV BCC refractory high-entropy alloy (VEC ≈ 4.68) and TiZrNbMoVx systems (VEC ≈ 4.7)
item.supporting_observation: The NbTaTiV HEA manifested almost perfectly isotropic elastic deformation at RT with a VEC of 4.68, similar to other isotropic alloys like Ti-V gum metals.
item.scope_limits: This correlation is based on theoretical calculations and limited experimental validation; the text notes that the validity of these theoretical methods is still under debate.
item.alternatives_considered: Conventional BCC alloys with narrow interatomic distance distributions and different VEC values that do not exhibit isotropy.
quotes: According to their calculations, the TiZrNbMo y V x [where (x, y) are (0, 0.9) and (0.5, 0.8)] refractory HEAs exhibit the elastically isotropic deformation behavior, which is strongly correlated to the value of the valence electron concentration (VEC).
Furthermore, these isotropic HEAs have a similar VEC of about 4.7 (in general, HEAs tend to form BCC solid-solution phases when VEC becomes less than 7.55).

item.mechanism: Resonant Ultrasound Spectroscopy (RUS) determines elastic constants by exciting a sample and detecting its resonant frequency response to identify eigenfrequencies.
item.operating_conditions: Frequency swept through 100- to 650-kHz range; sample corner-mounted between two transducers
item.supporting_observation: Large responses detected when the frequency corresponds to an eigenfrequency of the sample
item.scope_limits: Assumes elastic isotropy; relies on sample dimensions and observed resonances
quotes: one transducer excites the sample, while a receiving transducer detects and relays the sample's response of resonant frequencies
the frequency was swept through the 100- to 650-kHz range with large responses detected when the frequency corresponds to an eigenfrequency of the sample
elastic constants, ( C 11 , C 12 , and C 44 ), were determined, using sample dimensions, and observed resonances
